text:
mia: ran a sensitivity-matrix sweep across kernels for fp8 enablement. compared fp8 native kernel (h100/l40s) vs int8-gptq/awq fallbacks on atlas-13b. posting high-level notes + a small artifact link.

owen: nice, timeline? did you run both warm and cold kv-cache profiles?

mia: timeline: ~3h total. cold (empty KV) + hot (10k prefix) + longseq 8k tokens. sequences sampled from chat logs and unit eval prompts.

rachel: what metrics are we tracking?

mia: primary: ppl delta on eval set, top-1 token shift rate, and a small eval of exact-match QA where possible. also distributional churn (KL) vs fp32 baseline.

sasha: any catastrophic nans / infs?

mia: no NaNs. saw 0.03% token-level deviation leading to 0.4% EM drop on one configuration.

julian: which configuration caused that?

mia: FP8 kernel with tile=64, accumulate=fp16, and matrix-scale auto enabled on L40S. Specifically the kernel's per-channel scale quantization + autorescale path.

own: interesting — that's the tiling+autorescale interaction we worried about. did you repro on H100 with same kernel?

mia: repro on H100 showed smaller delta: 0.15% token shift, 0.2% EM. suspect L40S kernel path hits a different accumulation rounding (accumulate to FP16 vs FP32) + a slightly different vector width.

sasha: did you compare AWQ/GPTQ int8 variants?

mia: yes. GPTQ-int8 (standard) had better EM on the problematic set than FP8 in that L40S config — by ~0.6%. AWQ-int8 was between GPTQ and FP8. Important: FP8 still wins on latency / memory but accuracy trade-off is workload-dependent.

rachel: any 1-line mitigation?

mia: two quick mitigations: (1) force accumulate=fp32 on L40S for layers with high activation variance (detect via per-layer std > thresh), or (2) fallback routing: route requests with longprefix or few-shot inputs to the int8/GPTQ variant. Both keep latency SLOs ~within 5% for most traffic.

bench-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-inference-eng-ml/fp8-sensitivity-matrix/1755551234/ (contains csv heatmaps, per-layer traces, and a replay script)

owen: did you try disabling autorescale in kernel?

mia: yes — disabling autorescale removed the EM drop but caused a few tokens to clip in worst-case longseq (ppl spikes on tail). tradeoff.

sasha: can we add a cheap per-request heuristic to choose autorescale on/off? maybe based on input length or prompt-type tag?

julian: we have prompt-type from routing metadata for hosted traffic. simple: if prompt_type=="few_shot" and prefix_tokens>512 then prefer int8 route, else fp8.

mia: realistic decision: build a sensitivity matrix per-model that maps (prefix_len, avg_tok_entropy, batch_size) -> recommended profile {fp8_kernel_variant, fallback}. then console can surface a "recommended profile" per route.

own: how noisy is that matrix? do we need smoothing / clusterization?

mia: noisy at per-layer level, but aggregated per (prefix_bin, batch_bin) it's stable. used small gaussian smoothing on the heatmaps.

rachel: any perf numbers? latency / RPS?

mia: fp8 kernel on H100: median token latency ~6.2ms, throughput +35% vs int8-GPTQ. L40S fp8 median 7.8ms, throughput +28%. forcing accumulate=fp32 regresses latency by ~8-12% on L40S.

sasha: cost vs quality picture?

mia: cost wins for fp8 due to lower memory/less spilling; but if EM drop >0.5% on a critical eval, cost savings may not justify rollout. we flagged a set of "sensitivity-critical" test prompts where fp8 underperforms — recommend gating canary on those.

nowen: good. what's next? small action items pls.

mia: action items: 1) add per-layer std metric to onboarding profiler (owen). 2) wire the sensitivity matrix CSV into console so product can preview (rachel). 3) add a routing rule prototype for prefix_len heuristics (sasha). 4) schedule deeper bakeoff vs AWQ on additional models (julian).

own: i'll take item 1. quick question: thresholds?

own: propose std_thresh=0.08 for activations (empirical), fallback if layer_std>std_thresh & token_shift_rate>0.005.

mia: sounds good. i'll update the artifact README with those numbers.

rachel: will show a few heatmap screenshots in the weekly eng-ml sync.

sasha: can we also log the kernel variant id in traces so we can correlate production hits?

mia: yes — kernel_variant is already in trace metadata, will ensure it's surfaced in sample traces in the artifact.

julian: one more note: try a hybrid approach where KV cache ops use int8-gptq while matmuls use fp8 for new kernel handshake. might reduce the drift. low-risk prototype.

mia: noted, adding to bakeoff queue.

bench-bot: canary rollout created: canary-1755551234-fp8-sens-matrix (10% traffic, region:us-west2, fallback=int8-gptq).

own: ok let's monitor ppl & EM on the flagged prompt set for next 6 hours. i'll add an alert if EM drops >0.4%

mia: thanks all. quick summary posted in the artifact README. ping me for raw traces if you need to bisect further. :handshake:
